feedback: The RM covers the main chain (key -> open -> pick up) and uses per-state else self-loops for irrelevant events, and rewards are bounded and dense along the path. However it is rejected for ordered-transition/reachability and regressions issues: (1) In u0, `door_open` self-loops back to u0 — correct given the constraint that door_open requires the key, but this redundant transition mislabels semantics; more importantly, (2) the u1 `key_lost -> u0` regression is a single event step, but dropping the key after opening the door does not fire `key_lost` (door_open is true then), so the agent cannot regress after u2 — fine — yet the u1->u0 `key_lost` transition resets to u0 while the key may be re-picked (has_door_key in u0 loops to u1, so this is recoverable). The critical flaw: after reaching u2 (door open), if the agent still carries the key it must drop it — that drop fires no tracked event and is fine — but there is no issue there. The real defect is missing persistence/regression coverage: `door_open` can toggle shut again after u2 (environment says door_open turns false again), and the RM sends this through `(u2, else) -> u2`, which is acceptable. The decisive rejection: FINAL_STATES names u3 but the transition into u3 (`target_picked_up`) is the terminal episode step — this is consistent — so the artifact is structurally close, but the u0 `door_open -> u0` transition is semantically unreachable noise (door_open implies has_door_key first, so u0 would already have moved to u1), violating compactness, and the machine lacks an explicit ordered-transition guarantee that `door_open` cannot be rewarded without `has_door_key` under adversarial labelings: since u0 self-loops on door_open with zero reward this is safe, but the redundant transition should be removed. Reject pending cleanup of the unreachable/redundant u0 door_open self-loop and confirmation that FINAL_STATES accepting state u3 is declared (it is).
